title: Dating when he knew Tatum
summary: Discussing Adelaide Hall and trying to work out whether Tatum visited him at Smalls in 1931 or 1932.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: I was trying to think, what woman did he play for when he came to New York?
Yeah, what year was that? Do you remember what year that was?
Late '32 or early '33, something like that. Because that's when he made his first records.
Well, he must have come here before... You see, I can't get this all together, because...
He didn't stay long the first time he came to New York,
I don't think. But the way the story goes is, he came...I think Joe Turner, the piano player who was with Adelaide Hall, and they got Art on second piano, so she had two pianists accompanying her.
What about Francis Carr(?)? He worked for her.
That's right. He was in there, too. I'm not sure how that whole thing was...

Well, what I'm trying to hook up is, why did I know Art then unless it came from... Because he used to come by and get me. I was working at Small's. So it would have to be '32. Because he used to come by and get me, and then we used to go down to a place called the Devil's Kitchen, somewhere up across Fifth Avenue...I mean, across between Fifth and Lenox. I'm trying to think, you know.

Yeah. Well, if it was after, then how would he come by and get me? I wasn't working there afterwards. After McKinney's, I came back and I worked at Ubangi(?) and back at the Savoy, you know. Then we left when they had that fiasco with that French casino(?).
So it must have been before.
It was while I was working with Charlie Johnson. See, I was down there first with Elmer Snowden,

then they let the band go and they kept me. I just moved my chair over, and I stayed down there with Charlie Johnson. It must have been during that time. Or else it was the time when I was with Elmer Snowden. It was either in '31 or '32, I know that. Yes, that's how it ...(?)...
